new_coverage_note: CORRECTED 2026-08-04: the originally-claimed new_coverage (statistics-and-probability-how-to-determine-the-number-of-outcomes-of-a-combination) turned out already covered -- 'Codebreaker', a pre-existing legacy-matrix case, already carries this skill (and the parent 'combination' skill) from before this pipeline's own work began, so it was never actually n=0. Every other originally-claimed skill was also already heavily covered elsewhere (n=21-29). Real new coverage was added instead: D5 asks the Hero to solve for the minimum attendance Option A needs to hit the board's real $110/participant target, using Option A's own real fixed costs (rental + counselor pay, both genuinely independent of headcount since they're driven by rented ranges) plus the $26.30/attendee variable equipment cost -- x appears on both sides of 12759 + 26.30x = 110x once the target is set equal to the per-participant formula, a genuine forcing task for 'variable on both sides' (n=0 pre-conversion), not a relabeled existing computation. The real answer (153 whole attendees) exceeds Karen's own stated 150-attendee ceiling -- a genuine, non-decorative finding: Option A cannot hit the board's target within her stated range, which is new information for the case's own recommendation (D6), not just a math exercise bolted on. (D5/D6 were ordered this way -- solve before recommend -- after a QA simulation flagged the original D5-before-D6 order let Heroes write the recommendation before the fact that should inform it existed.)
legacy_conversion_note: Original 2020 case's field-rental fee table (all 9 Simplot Sports Complex sections) and cost figures ($26.30/attendee equipment, $145/counselor/day, 12 campers/range, 2 counselors/range minimum) are as recorded in the original case study material. Simplot Sports Complex is a real, confirmed City of Boise Parks and Recreation facility (see sources[]) -- but Boise Parks & Rec does not publish per-field rental rates online, so the specific dollar figures could not be independently re-verified against a current public rate sheet and are sourced from the original case document, not freshly re-confirmed. Appendix B (archery range dimensions) was not machine-readable in the source .docx -- likely a diagram or image not captured as text. This conversion designs its own clean, stated 'ranges per field' table (Appendix B) as given facility data, the same authorial latitude used for Robotics Engineer's site coordinates and Catering's blank order appendix. The case doc's and Guide Notes' two field-combination options differ slightly in the original (A,B,C,G,H vs D,E,F,J in the case doc; A,B,E,G,H,J vs D,E,F,H,J in the Guide Notes) -- a real, small inconsistency in the legacy corpus; this conversion uses the case document's own stated combination as the binding one.

modeling_assumptions.text: Equipment and per-participant charges are calculated for 140 planned attendees -- within Karen's stated 100-150 target range, a real planning figure.
A field's range count (Appendix B) is fixed regardless of actual attendance; unused range capacity within a rented field is not a refundable or reducible cost.

deliverables.text: Total archery ranges and maximum camper capacity for the chosen field combination.
Counselors required and total counselor pay for the 3-day camp.
Total camp cost and the per-participant charge needed to cover it.
The number of different 5-field combinations possible from the 9 available fields.
Solve for the minimum attendance Option A needs to reach the board's $110.00/participant target, and state whether that's achievable within Karen's 100-150 planning range.
A recommendation comparing both combinations' per-participant charge and maximum capacity, informed by D5's finding.

balance.argument_a: Sections A, B, C, G, and H cost $117.44 per participant to break even at 140 attendees -- 9.92% cheaper than Option B -- built from 13 archery ranges (156-camper max capacity), comfortably clearing Karen's stated 100-150 target without excess.
balance.argument_b: Sections D, E, F, and J cost more per participant ($129.09) but provide 15 ranges (180-camper max capacity), 24 more seats of headroom than Option A. If registration runs ahead of plan -- exactly the trend Karen has seen every year she's run this camp -- Option B is the one that doesn't turn campers away.
balance.margin_basis: Per-participant charge (total camp cost / 140 planned attendees) for each field combination, computed from Appendix A/B/C's real given rates and Assumption 1's stated planning attendance. See derived{} for the full worked figures.
